Buchanan via Aristotle: forethought in making = the master art that became 'design'
Heidegger: essence of craft is the relationship to material, not tool-facility
hands as bodily site of making AND thinking; thought/speech/hand coupled
design as active coping with thrown-ness (Oosterling); fort-da
Merleau-Ponty: speech does not translate ready-made thought but accomplishes it
Heidegger: empathy is grounded in Being-with, not its constituting bridge
craft = designer/maker/user the same; design = modern, division-of-labor split of planning from making
reasoning toward what could be; flash of insight (Peirce); future-oriented, intuitive
sciences/humanities/design differ in phenomenon, method, values
Tonkinwise/Dreyfus: expertise = tacit-ed bodily activity articulable only after the act
Schön: thinking-while-acting links theory and practice into one praxical movement
Rittel/Webber: defy definition, multi-force, no clear end; need experiential models

claims.text: Thinking inherently involves making; we think only through making (externalization is necessary).
Design = forethought, the architectonic 'master art' of making (Buchanan via Aristotle).
The essence of craft is relatedness to materials; for experience design the material is experience.
The capacity to design depends on two bodily capabilities: speech and the hands.
Empathy is grounded in being-with rather than constituting the first bridge between subjects.
Design is a modern phenomenon: the division of labor split planning (design) from making (craft).
Abduction is the logic of design: reasoning toward what could be.
A phenomenological point of view is the next evolution of design thinking.
Wicked problems require rigorous study of human experience, which phenomenology supplies.
